newsitem.title: ITALY: "Thank you Italy", says reprieved death row man.
newsitem.headline: "Thank you Italy", says reprieved death row man.

text.p: A U.S. prisoner on death row who won an 11th hour stay of execution thanked Italy on Wednesday for championing his cause with a wave of protests and appeals for clemency from the Vatican, human rights groups and politicians.
"I am so happy and elated that I'm speechless," Joseph O'Dell told state radio RAI by telephone from jail in Virginia.
"I've come within 24 hours of dying and I just want to thank all the wonderful people in Italy..who showed such compassion and love. It's something I'm not used to seeing," he said.
O'Dell, 55, was convicted in 1986 of the rape and murder of 44-year-old secretary Helen Schartner and had been due to die by lethal injection on Wednesday night.
The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a temporary stay of execution for O'Dell, who claims new DNA evidence casts doubt on his murder conviction.
The reprieve will remain in effect until the court rules on O'Dell's appeal challenging his conviction and sentence.
O'Dell's case, which had received scant attention in the United States, has stirred passions in Italy, which is in the forefront of international campaigns to end capital punishment.
Italy claimed much of the credit on Wednesday for the Court's move, which came after a wave of appeals led by Pope John Paul. The Vatican said it was satisfied at the decision.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who had appealed to U.S. President Bill Clinton, told La Repubblica newspaper that as a Roman Catholic he was profoundly opposed to the death penalty and believed the doubts in O'Dell's case needed to be studied.
"I couldn't be silent, I had to act. And that's what I did, like so many others," he said, adding he was happy if Italian and Vatican pressure had helped achieve the stay of execution.

Opponents of the death penalty turned their planned protest outside the U.S. embassy on Tuesday night into a joyous rally, waving placards saying "Thank You". Italian deputies interrupted a debate in parliament to applaud when the news broke.
O'Dell's wife, Lori Urs, told Italian state television she believed the "marvellous compassion" Italy showed had helped.
But La Repubblica said that "the great wave of Italian self congratulation" should not forget that another man, Ronnie Lee Hoke, 39, was executed in Virginia on Tuesday.
